Me, I am an old man of 58 years, and this small piece of land I am farming is not mine — I am only renting it. So I cannot spend too much money on it, because the owner can take it back. The rains here in Tabora come only once, from November, so I must prepare well with my hoe. I don't have money for fertilizer from the shop, but I keep a few goats and chickens, so their manure I will carry to the field. The seed I will use is the one I saved from last year, like my father taught me — the shop seed is expensive and I don't trust it on rented land.

For pests, if the insects come bad I may buy a small bottle from the agrovet, but usually I just pick them by hand or leave it. Water, there is no irrigation here — we wait for God's rain. Me and my wife and one son who is still at home will do most of the work, but for clearing and weeding when the rains are heavy, I will call two or three neighbours and pay them small money or give them food.
